title: How to photograph paintings and drawings faithfully with a phone
description: Record two-dimensional artwork with even light, straight geometry and a separate detail view, without turning the reproduction into a creative edit.
summary: Record two-dimensional artwork with even light, straight geometry and a separate detail view, without turning the reproduction into a creative edit.
quickAnswer: Position the phone square to the artwork, illuminate the whole surface evenly and include all four edges in a reference frame. Check a center detail and the corners before moving anything. Make a faithful full-work photograph first, then separate detail images for texture, signatures or condition.

sections.title: Choose a record of the work before a styled photograph
paragraphs: A portfolio image should let the viewer assess the artwork. A studio photograph may instead show the work, room and artist together. Make those different pictures intentionally. Do not use a dramatic room view as the only record of a painting whose colors and proportions matter.

List the required files before setting up: full work, one texture detail and a signature or condition view if relevant. Record the title and dimensions in your notes so they remain associated with the correct files during editing.

sections.title: Align the phone with the work itself
paragraphs: The University of Iowa recommends even light and aligning a two-dimensional work with the camera frame; larger work can be photographed on a neutral wall. Smith College advises centering the camera at the artwork’s midpoint. Keep the phone’s image plane parallel to the surface, including any tilt in the work.

For a rectangular painting, compare opposite sides in your preview. If one side appears much shorter, adjust the camera position before cropping. Leave a small border in a reference image so you can verify the shape later. Avoid a very tight capture that conceals an accidentally missing corner.

sections.title: Check the full surface for glare and uneven light
paragraphs: Iowa advises against the phone’s built-in flash for documenting artwork. If you use two lights, Smith College describes placing them to either side and adjusting their positions to avoid reflections. Its camera-specific aperture and lens settings are not universal phone settings.

Inspect several points rather than judging the center alone: top, bottom, both sides and a region with subtle color. A bright patch that moves when the light moves is a capture problem to solve before editing. On glossy or framed work, try another lighting position instead of making the whole image darker.

Do not unframe a fragile work or touch its surface just to remove glare. If you cannot make an acceptable record with a safe setup, use a specialist reproduction service or document the limitation alongside the image.

sections.title: Use a consistent capture and review sequence

items.title: Full reference.
items.text: Include the entire work and a narrow surrounding border. Keep this frame even if the final submission requires a closer crop.

items.title: Geometry check.
items.text: Compare straight edges and corners in the saved file. Correct the physical setup if a large adjustment would be needed.

items.title: Detail check.
items.text: Inspect a fine mark in the center and near a corner. A sharp center alone is not enough for a faithful full-work reproduction.

items.title: Separate detail image.
items.text: Photograph texture or a signature with its own framing. Keep its filename associated with the full-work image.

sections.title: Edit to match the object, not a fashionable look
paragraphs: Compare the capture with the work in a stable viewing situation. Do not increase saturation simply because the phone display makes the picture feel subdued. If a color is important to an application or print, a casual screen comparison is not a substitute for a controlled color workflow.

Keep an untouched capture and a delivery copy. Record any perspective correction or significant color adjustment. Cropping a border is different from removing a mark that belongs to the work. For a submission, follow its actual file and framing requirements rather than assuming every portfolio wants the same format.

faq.question: Is this the same as scanning an old printed photograph?
faq.answer: No. A large painting or drawing requires attention to its plane, surface, illumination and faithful appearance. A detail view may need different light from the full-work record.

faq.question: Can I use Portrait mode to blur the wall?
faq.answer: For a reproduction, start with a normal photograph that preserves the work’s boundaries. Make a separate styled image if you want a more decorative presentation.
